title: The constant group scheme T_E and the group law on its T-valued points
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ an abelian group. The *constant group scheme* $T_E$ with value $E$ over $T$ is the coproduct $T_E=\coprod_{e\in E}T$ of copies of $T$ indexed by $E$, with coprojections $\iota_e:T\to T_E$ (the coproduct exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]), made a $T$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base] by the structure morphism $\pi:T_E\to T$ with $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_T$ for all $e$ (the codiagonal, given by the universal property of the coproduct). Write $V_e=\iota_e(T)\subseteq T_E$ for the *components* (open and closed, pairwise disjoint and covering $T_E$, by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]). Let $P=T_E\times_TT_E$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $\pi$ with itself, with projections $p,q$ and structure morphism $\rho=\pi\circ p=\pi\circ q:P\to T$, and put $W_{e,e'}=p^{-1}(V_e)\cap q^{-1}(V_{e'})$ for $e,e'\in E$. The *multiplication* $m:P\to T_E$ is the morphism of schemes whose restriction to $W_{e,e'}$, regarded as an open subscheme of $P$ [def-weil-open-immersion], is $\iota_{e+e'}\circ\rho|_{W_{e,e'}}$ for all $(e,e')\in E\times E$. That the $W_{e,e'}$ are open and closed, pairwise disjoint and cover $P$, that such an $m$ exists and is unique (gluing along this cover, [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], the overlaps being empty), and that $\pi\circ m=\rho$ and $m(W_{e,e'})\subseteq V_{e+e'}$, is the statement node lem-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme-multiplication (recorded in `pointers`), from which this definition takes $m$. For a $T$-scheme $s:U\to T$ and $T$-morphisms $f,g:U\to T_E$, the *sum* is $f+g:=m\circ(f,g):U\to T_E$, where $(f,g):U\to P$ is the morphism with $p\circ(f,g)=f$ and $q\circ(f,g)=g$ (it exists since $\pi\circ f=s=\pi\circ g$); the *constant point* attached to $e\in E$ is $c_e:=\iota_e\circ s:U\to T_E$. The map $E\to\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,T_E)$, $e\mapsto c_e$, is the *canonical map*. (The name follows Stacks Tag 03YW, where $(T_E,m)$ is a group scheme over $T$; the group-scheme axioms for $m$ are not part of this definition and are not claimed here.)

source.place: Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW, label example-constant-group): $G_S$ is the base change of $\coprod_{g\in G}\Spec(\mathbf Z)$, with the multiplication mapping the component of $(g,g')$ to the component of $gg'$; Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5, label remark-constant-locally-constant-maps). Here written directly over $T$ (the base change of $\coprod_g\Spec\mathbf Z$ to $T$ is $\coprod_gT$), with the components $W_{e,e'}$ of the fibre product described as open subsets

proof.text: *The data are well formed.* $E$ is a set, so the coproduct $\coprod_{e\in E}T$ exists with coprojections $\iota_e$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and its universal property applied to the family $(\mathrm{id}_T)_{e\in E}$ gives the unique $\pi$ with $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_T$; so $(T_E,\pi)$ is a $T$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. The fibre product $P$ of $\pi$ with itself exists [def-pc-fibre-product] and $\pi\circ p=\pi\circ q$ by its commutative square, so $\rho$ is well defined. For $T$-morphisms $f,g:U\to T_E$ we have $\pi\circ f=s=\pi\circ g$, so the universal property of $P$ gives the unique $(f,g)$ with $p\circ(f,g)=f$, $q\circ(f,g)=g$. $c_e=\iota_e\circ s$ is a $T$-morphism: $\pi\circ\iota_e\circ s=s$. The morphism $m$ is not constructed here: its existence and uniqueness, and the facts about the $W_{e,e'}$ it rests on, are the statement node lem-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme-multiplication (a pointer, not a dependency).
